ai.title: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 adds keychain auth and server model catalog
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI now stores its auth token in the OS credential store (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or Linux Secret Service) via `Bun.secrets` instead of the plain `credentials.json` file, driven by the new `loadStoredAuthToken` startup call and `auth-token-store` module, with the token falling back to the file if the keychain is unavailable. Simultaneously, the CLI introduces a server-driven model catalog protocol (`freebuff-model-catalog.ts`) where models are referenced by opaque rotating handles rather than compiled-in IDs, with a new single root agent `base3-free-catalog` built at runtime from catalog rows, plus a `FreebuffModelPolicyOverlay` seam allowing the server to override pricing, session limits, and effort ladders without client releases. The version is bumped from 0.2.3 to 0.2.4 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/index.tsx`, `loadStoredAuthToken` is called before credential reads to initialize a new OS keychain-backed token store (`cli/src/utils/auth-token-store.ts`) for Freebuff, while `agents/base3.ts` and `common/src/types/freebuff-model-catalog.ts` introduce a server-driven model catalog protocol and a new `base3-free-catalog` root agent.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 0.2.4 moves your login credentials into your operating system's built-in password store instead of leaving them in a readable file, reducing the risk that other programs on your computer can access them. If your device's password store is unavailable, such as on a remote server, your login safely remains in a private file so you are not locked out. The release also adds a server-driven model catalog, allowing the app to display new or updated AI models and their specific settings without needing to download a new version of the software. The CLI now automatically fetches this list at startup, meaning you can use newly available models immediately as soon as they are published by the service.

ai.summary: The CLI auth module in cli now deduplicates credentials read and parse error logs by tracking distinct failure signatures in a process-local Set. ai.title: Device key signing and scheduled row filtering for Freebuff catalog
ai.summary: Freebuff's server model catalog now supports device-bound request signing and scheduled model launches. A per-install Ed25519 key pair signs catalog GET, session, and completions requests in catalog mode via new `FREEBUFF_DEVICE_KEY_HEADER`, `FREEBUFF_DEVICE_TIMESTAMP_HEADER`, and `FREEBUFF_DEVICE_SIGNATURE_HEADER` headers, registered with the server at `FREEBUFF_DEVICE_KEYS_PATH`. Model catalog rows with an `opensAt` timestamp later than the catalog's `issuedAt` are filtered out before being held in memory, ensuring the client never lists, selects, or sends a model that has not yet launched. The SDK's completions path now accepts a `requestHeaders` hook so the CLI can attach the fetch id and device signature to every model request.

ai.title: CLI streak status labels odd-hour resets as your time
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI release 0.2.7 adds a "(your time)" label to streak reset times that do not fall on midnight, addressing reports that users east of Pacific time misread odd-hour streak day turnovers as server time.
